title: Chapter 761
paragraphs: Chapter 761
Episode 187. The People We Need to Find, Unexpected Clues (2)
Another six days have passed.
Thanks to the disclosure of records by the Vamel Union, people of the world now knew all the secrets behind the Hall of Abominations.
"...Diphus Runcandel and Lin Milcano's deaths are being covered up."
At the Lutero Magic Federation, Tower of Tales.
Octavia looked over the newspaper on her desk and spoke.
The newspaper described the disclosed records of the Hall of Abominations.
-<Diphus Runcandel shared the power of the abomination with Mary Runcandel and Jin Runcandel, pinning their hopes on them.>
-<On May 22, 1803, Diphus Runcandel left the world with a piece of the abomination's power. The abomination weakened.>
The Runcandel columnists, led by Dino Jagerlun, did not attempt to restore Diphus' honor through these records.
They merely transferred the records into articles in a matter-of-fact tone.
Because Mary didn't want it.
The death of Diphus was a matter of personal commemoration as his closest brother.
Regardless of the hope he pinned on Jin or the reasons he had to do so, the fact that many people died by his corrupted hand did not disappear.
Nevertheless, people were understanding Diphus through the phrase 'hoping on Jin Runcandel.'
Of course, not everyone did, but at least Diphus was no longer treated as an irreplaceable traitor.
The same was true for Lin Milcano's betrayal.
From the start, Lin's betrayal was not known to the public or even to their temporary allies, but the fact that she chose to play the villain for the Hall of Abominations was now coming to light.
"Our reporters are trying to continue to find faults through Ran, Vigo, Myu, and Anne, but it's not easy to change the atmosphere."
The betrayals of the revived previous generation leaders, and the exploits of those who did not corrupt until the end, were also receiving a lot of public support.
In this way, the disclosed records, from one to ten, were mostly bringing beneficial effects to the Runcandel.
"Moreover, Lin Milcano's betrayal wasn't even told to us at the time. Although the Hall of Abominations did end in victory..."
When Ronil responded, Kadun grinded his teeth.

"It's a blatant deception! The 12th flagbearer, that damned guy played us. He proceeded with the information disclosure without even consulting us, it's infuriating. He backstabs us like this? Even if we chew him out, it won't be satisfying...!"
At Kadun's words, Veradin, who had been listening quietly, lowered his head in silence.
"Getting angry won't solve anything, Mr. Kadun. Calm your excitement. It's embarrassing every time you act like this."
As soon as Veradin's words ended, the atmosphere in the conference room dropped chillingly cold.
Since becoming the guardian dragon of Kelliark, no one had ever scolded Kadun like this.
Even Kelliark would always soothe him when Kadun was angry or talking nonsense.
"...What did you say?"

"If you intend to express your anger and make the listeners uncomfortable, you need the ability to back it up. Do you, Mr. Kadun, have the power to pressure the Runcandel and Vamel Union right now? Can you crush them with your own power?"
Kadun glared at Veradin.
After regaining his rationality, Veradin was moving away from the way Zipple knew him, and the way they wanted him through mind manipulation.
"A minor clan head, even your father didn't dare to disrespect me."
"So, what are you suggesting? Is there any reason why I should follow my father's attitude towards you, Mr. Kadun? I don't think I said anything wrong."
"Veradin!"

"Please refrain from unnecessarily expressing your emotions and ruining the atmosphere in the future. It just looks ridiculous to both allies and enemies. As the guardian dragon of the clan, you should have a sense of weight. I think I've said something similar before."
Just as Kadun was about to shout something, Octavia and Ronil stopped him.
"If you don't like my way, go ahead and recover my father right away. Then, I will respect you more, Mr. Kadun."
Bang!
In the end, Kadun smashed the table and left the conference room.
"Ronil, warn Mr. Kadun after the meeting. If he leaves in the middle of a meeting like this again, he won't have a chance to sit here again."
"...Understood."
"Have we received a response from the Vamel Union regarding the use of the purifier?"

-'I will also need Kelliark's power at the decisive moment. Of course, it's unpleasant, but if the purifier is improved before the final battle, and if the power of Kelliark Zipple is absolutely necessary, then I will use the purifier on him.'
This was what Jin said during the temporary alliance talks.
As soon as the war ended, Zipple requested the use of the purifier from Runcandel.
"Not yet. There hasn't even been a response."
"It seems they have no intention to agree."
"Should we request more strongly?"
"No, it's okay. It doesn't seem like my father's condition can be treated with their purifier anyway, so it would be better to find another way. Ask Mr. Kadun to take care of that."

"......Veradin. No, head of clan. It doesn't seem good to overly neglect Mr. Kadun. Runcandel and the Vamel Union are firmly united right after the war, isn't there no need to deliberately create a rift among us?"

"Ghost Commander, our federation also needs the competent side of Mr. Kadun for unity. Not only that, it applies to all of the clan's executive members including myself. They have a certain focal point, Jin Runcandel."
"I trust it is not your intention to break Mr. Kadun's momentum and reveal your dignity to the subordinates."
"That is something to consider. If Mr. Kadun becomes polite, my command will be re-proven to the clan and subordinate forces."
"Clan Head."

"Enough, let's stop the discussion here. Ghost Commander, consult with the secretaries to find a way to disrupt the atmosphere in Runcandel. Ran and Vuco, Myu An. Rather than using them, it would be better to arrange a skeleton that Jin Runcandel is instigating a new war right after the demon war. After all, they are really irritating us and Kinzelo."
"......Understood."

"We have received reports that a shipyard is being built near the second star of the Hairan Empire. Keep an eye on this part, Octavia. Steel is likely to be the most scarce, so the problem needs to be continually pressured."

"The Lutero Federation has stopped steel exports and is checking all transportation methods from the Post-War Kingdom, neighboring neutral countries, and Hufepesuto. Just like you said, Clan Head, it seems to be struggling."
"That alone cannot be reassuring. There is a high possibility of having a back pocket somewhere. It's probably Minche's Association... or Kinzelo."

"The former is being monitored continuously. Hufepesuto, the Vamel Union, and the Imperial transport ships have not been spotted yet. Plus, the 12th class hurt their pride. Since we are renting weapons made by the Association without permission, they will not help easily."
"What about Kinzelo?"
"Kashmir Alfryon from the Vamel Union visited the new headquarters this morning."
"It would be difficult to detect transport through the commander's dimensional gate."
"I will confirm whether their deal was made when I meet them."
"Whether it was made or failed. By all means, offer better conditions than the Vamel Union to turn the deal to our side."
The meeting ended after a few more items were discussed.
Veradin sat quietly for a moment in the meeting room everyone had left.
'......Pressuring Mr. Kadun was definitely necessary, but it was excessive.'
In fact, Veradin had felt for some time that his emotions were not properly controlled.
Provoking Kadun just now was a planned action, but it felt like the words went too far than he thought.
'Is it because of my father, or because of the authority obtained through the traces of magical power. Control is not easy.'
Soon, Veradin slowly moved his steps to the top floor of the tower.
"......Father."
Veradin, placing his hand on Kelliark's preservation device.
Inside the preservation device, Kelliark had turned completely dark.
Body modification had already progressed, making regeneration impossible with the current purifier.
"Soon, I will be able to get you out of there. Then perhaps......"
Veradin leaned closer to the preservation device and whispered the rest of his words.
"I will leave now. Please rest comfortably."
As Veradin left.
Kelliark quietly opened his eyes.
With eyes as lifeless as black stones, he stared at the door that Veradin had exited through for a long time.
Once in a while, his fingers twitched.
For the past six days, Jin met with the kings and lords of various regions in Hufepesuto, the heads of allied clans, and immigrants to give them encouragement.
Construction of the shipyard in Geomhwangji was also going smoothly.
Knowing that steel was also needed for the construction of the shipyard, the blacksmiths of the Association had already started sending Baelram.
Even Veradin had not thought of transporting via Baelram.
Even when Zipple was having a meeting, Baelram was tirelessly, leisurely carrying steel.
Kashmir's visit to Kinzelo's new headquarters, along with the construction of a shipyard near the second star of Hairan, was a deception.
Kashmir intentionally proposed a steel deal to Kinzelo, and was rejected.
It was natural since he just wanted to buy steel at a price higher than the market price.
While the shipyard near the second star of Hairan will actually be used when completed, the core of the union shipbuilding was the secret shipyard in Geomhwangji.
After receiving all reports related to that, Jin, along with Valeria and Bale, had returned to the Caldoran tundra.
[You've come, youngest one. I see Bale and Lady Valeria again...... Lady Valeria, I was sorry then. As you know, I was not normal.]
"That's alright."
Short greetings were exchanged, and Valeria reviewed the record of the words the woman in question had said.
Fortunately, the record was immediately confirmed without any hesitation.
<Luntia Runcandel refuses a contract with Lokia Ganesto.>
<'If Chiron Runcandel returns as he is, your brother won't be able to handle him. Without my help, never.'>
For a long time, the party could not take their eyes off that passage.
